title: Grade Calculation Methodology
overview: Grade calculations convert raw scores to letter grades or determine what score is needed on remaining work to achieve a target grade. Different institutions use different grading scales.

methods.name: Standard US Grading Scale
methods.description: The most common grading scale in US education, mapping percentage scores to letter grades.

formula.name: Standard Scale
formula.description: Plus/minus grades divide each range into thirds

methods.name: Plus/Minus Grading Scale
methods.description: Further divides letter grades to provide more precision. Typically adds ±3% from letter grade boundaries.

formula.name: Plus/Minus Scale
formula.description: Note: A+ is often 97+ when used

methods.name: Curved Grading
methods.description: Adjusts grades based on class performance. Can be additive (add points to all) or normative (grade on distribution).

formula.name: Curve Methods
formula.expression:
Additive: Final = Raw + Curve Points

Normative: A = top 10-15%, B = next 20-25%, etc.

Square Root: Final = √(Raw × 100)

methods.accuracy: Depends on method and class distribution
limitations: Normative curves pit students against each other
May inflate or deflate grades unfairly

methods.name: Required Score Calculation
methods.description: Calculate what score is needed on remaining assignments to achieve a target final grade.

formula.name: Needed Score Formula
formula.expression: Needed = (Target × Total Weight - Current × Earned Weight) / Remaining Weight

footnotes: Letter grades date back to Harvard in 1883
Pass/Fail (P/F) is common for electives and pandemic semesters
Medical schools often use Pass/Fail or Honors/Pass/Fail
UK/Europe use different systems (First Class, 2:1, 2:2, Third, Fail)
disclaimer: Grading scales vary by institution and instructor. Check your syllabus for the specific scale used in your course.
